London, 25th February 2009
Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest
African Rainbow Minerals announced that platinum’s contribution to group headline earnings was a 
negative R293m from a positive R206m a year ago.  ARM is not planning to cut platinum ounces by more 
than the planned 10%. Attributable PGM production increased by 14% to 153,157 oz.  ARM’s platinum 
division paid off debt to ARM Mining Consortium 18 months ahead of schedule.   It is curtailing a number 
of plans to grow production in efforts to conserve cash.  At the Modikwa mine, (41.5% shareholder with 
Anglo Platinum), mining of the Merensky reef has been stopped as has work on deepening declines.  
Approval of a completed feasibility study into the phase two UG2 replacement project has been delayed to 
save capital expenditure.  The Two Rivers mine will process stockpiled material to partially replace more 
expensive underground ore over “the next few months”. Nkomati’s tonnes milled increased by 47% while 
nickel production increased to 2,495 tonnes from 2,367 tonnes in the comparable period. 
Source:  Mining Mx 
Aquarius Platinum expects to publish details by the end of March on plans to reﬁnance a R1,5-billion 
(about $150-million) bridge loan, and will announce a ﬁrm offer for Aim-listed Ridge Mining at the 
same time, CEO Stuart Murray said.  The ﬁrm is seeking to reﬁnance the bridge loan facility from Rand 
Merchant Bank, which falls due on June 30 this year.  The debt will be reﬁnanced in rand terms.  Aquarius 
said two weeks ago that it planned to offer one of its own shares in exchange for every 2,75 Ridge shares 
in issue.  Although 2009 is likely to be a time for “hunkering down”, the company will continue to look for 
smallish acquisition opportunities, and  ways to co-operate with its neighbours.
Source: Mining Weekly 
North American Palladium, for the year ended December 31, 2008, reported a net loss of $160.7 
million or $1.94/share compared to a net loss of $28.7 million or $0.51/share for the year ended 
December 31, 2007.  Palladium production for Q408 of 21,373 ounces was down 70% compared to 
71,595 ounces in Q407, mainly to the temporary closure of the Lac des Iles mine in October 08. Palladium 
production for 2008 was 212,046 ounces, down 26% compared to 286,334 ounces in 2007.  For Q408, 
cash cost/oz of palladium, net of by-product metal revenues and royalties, increased to US$464/oz, 
versus US$221/oz in Q407 due primarily to decreased by-product revenues as a result of lower by-
product commodity prices, offset by the weakening Canadian dollar. For 2008, cash cost/oz of palladium, 
net of by-product metal revenues and royalties, increased to US$283/oz compared to US$164/oz in2007. 
Source:  North American Palladium
Zimbabwe Platinum Mines revealed that it needs an extra $60 million as it looks to increase its 
production through projects at its Ngezi Mine.  Having already secured an $80 million loan facility, the 
miner is now attempting to get further support to help it increase production capacity from 2.1 million 
tonnes per year to 4.2 million tonnes per year.  Zimbabwe Platinum Mines reported in its interim results 
for the six months to 31st December 2008 that its sales volumes were up by 15 per cent.
Source:  Herald
General Motors, already surviving on $13.4 billion in U.S. aid, will probably report a fourth straight 
annual loss tomorrow as Chief Executive Ofﬁcer Rick Wagoner asks the Treasury for more cash to ﬁnish 
the year. GM is seeking the remaining $4.6 billion it requested in an $18 billion plea Dec. 2 as well as $4.5 
billion to pay off a revolving loan scheduled for repayment in 2011. GM said a failure of the economy to 
improve over the next two years may mean the automaker will need another $7.5 billion. 
Source:  Bloomberg
